statement: In [1], Akrida et al. restricted the problem to temporal cliques, i.e. temporal graphs with a complete underlying graph, with unique time labels, but did not improve the asymptotic density of spanners. Furthering the work, in 2021, Casteigts et al. [8] proved that temporal cliques admit sparse spanners with O(n log n) edges, and designed an algorithm to find such a spanner. The question of whether a linear spanner exists in all temporal cliques remains open. A study of the problem on random temporal graphs is done by Casteigts et al. in [9] to establish sharp thresholds on connectivity properties and the implications for the existence of different kinds of sparse spanners. In [2] Angrick et al. make a considerable step forward by proving the existence of linear spanners in some families of temporal cliques, leaving very constrained cases where the question is still open. Other research on spanners include robustness [5], or inefficient networks [11].
context: As mentioned earlier, another area of interest in temporal graphs is the study of spanners, i.e. subgraphs that preserve connectivity. It is first introduced by Kempe et al. [16], as an open question about finding a sparse subset of edges in an already connected graph. A negative answer was given by Axiotis and Fotakis [3], showing that there are minimal connected temporal graphs with Θ(n2 ) edges. Additionally, they investigate weaker connectivity requirements, as the total connectivity is sometimes not relevant in practical applications. Our work also considers such generalizations. In [1], Akrida et al. restricted the problem to temporal cliques, i.e. temporal graphs with a complete underlying graph, with unique time labels, but did not improve the asymptotic density of spanners. Furthering the work, in 2021, Casteigts et al. [8] proved that temporal cliques admit sparse spanners with O(n log n) edges, and designed an algorithm to find such a spanner. The question of whether a linear spanner exists in all temporal cliques remains open. A study of the problem on random temporal graphs is done by Casteigts et al. in [9] to establish sharp thresholds on connectivity properties and the implications for the existence of different kinds of sparse spanners. In [2] Angrick et al. make a considerable step forward by proving the existence of linear spanners in some families of temporal cliques, leaving very constrained cases where the question is still open. Other research on spanners include robustness [5], or inefficient networks [11]. 2 Preliminaries and notation This section introduces important definitions and makes some basic observations that contextualize our problem. ▶ Definition 1 (temporal graph). A temporal graph is a pair (G, λ) where G = (V, E) is a (static) graph and λ : E → 2N . λ(e) represents the set of time steps where edge e is present. The lifespan of the graph is T = maxe∈E max λ(e). (G, λ) is simple if |λ(e)| = 1 for all e ∈ E. A temporal graph is also classically defined using temporal edges. A temporal edge is a pair (e, t) with e ∈ V2 and t ∈ N \ {0}. Then the temporal edges of (G, λ) are the temporal edges (e, t) where e ∈ E and t ∈ λ(e). The snapshot of (G, λ) at time t is the (static) graph Gt = (V, Et ) where Et is the set of edges e ∈ E with t ∈ λ(e) (i.e., temporal edges at time t). We will call snapshot components at time t the set of connected components of the snapshot at time t. ▶ Definition 2 (journey). A journey (or temporal path) of a temporal graph G is a sequence (u0 , u1 , t0 ), (u1 , u2 , t1 ), . . . , (uk−1 , uk , tk−1 ) where: ({ui , ui+1 }, ti ) is a temporal edge of G; ti ≤ ti+1 (resp. ti < ti+1 ) if the journey is non-strict (resp. strict). ▶ Definition 3 (temporal connectivity). A vertex v is reachable from u if there is a journey from u to v (denoted u → v). If every vertex v is reachable from every other vertex u in G, then G is temporally connected. If all journeys are strict, then the graph is strictly connected. ▶ Definition 4 (augmentation). Let G be a temporal graph, and F be a set of temporal edges. The augmentation of G by F is the temporal graph denoted G ↑ F obtained from G by adding the temporal edges in F . We say that F is a (strictly) connecting set for G if G ↑ F is (strictly) connected. Now we can formally define the main problems under consideration. Temporal Connectivity Augmentation (TCA) Input: A temporal graph G, a set F of temporal edges and an integer K.
